questions.q: In the manufacturing company scenario, why is a Payables account rule for Freight that only covers "Domestic" freight a design risk?
options: It is not a risk; Domestic is the only freight category that ever matters
Because, as seen in lesson 25's scenario, a supplier base that includes international freight needs the rule to cover every category actually in use, or Create Accounting will error
Because Freight should never be its own journal line type
Because account rules cannot reference freight categories at all
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly echoes lesson 25's troubleshooting scenario: a Freight rule covering only Domestic will fail on international freight invoices.

questions.q: Why are supplier-number supporting references described as essential for this manufacturing company's Payables design?
options: They are not essential; supporting references are optional decoration
Because supporting references replace the need for account rules
Because supplier numbers are required by the Chart of Accounts
Because with hundreds of suppliers, the company needs the Open Account Balances Listing to know what is owed to each individual supplier
questions.explain: Supporting references carrying supplier number enable the Open Account Balances Listing to break the AP Trade balance down by individual supplier.

questions.q: Why would a mapping set be a better fit than many individual account rule conditions for the Fixed Assets design, given a large equipment base?
options: Mapping sets cannot be used with Fixed Assets
Mapping sets eliminate the need for a Chart of Accounts
A mapping set translating equipment category into the Natural Account segment avoids building a separate rule condition for every one of dozens of categories
Account rules are not permitted on Fixed Assets event classes
questions.explain: A mapping set keeps the category-to-account translation centralized and maintainable, rather than requiring dozens of individual rule conditions.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say Cash Management reconciliation quality depends on "everything upstream"?
options: Because Cash Management has nothing to do with AP or AR accounting

Because Cash Management reconciles bank activity against AP payments and AR receipts that were already accounted through SLA, so correct upstream account rules and supporting references directly determine how clean that reconciliation is
Because Cash Management never actually uses Subledger Accounting
Because reconciliation is unrelated to accuracy of account rules
questions.explain: Cash Management reconciliation depends on the accuracy of AP and AR accounting already produced by SLA, tying the whole design together.

questions.q: What course comes next in the Oracle Fusion Financials Consultant path after Oracle Fusion Subledger Accounting, according to this lesson's outro?
options: Oracle Fusion Security
Oracle Fusion Procure-to-Pay
SQL for Oracle Financials
Oracle Financial Reporting
questions.explain: The outro names Oracle Financial Reporting as the next course, which is the first course in the path's "Reporting & Data" stage.
